# Opal Pettigrew

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028)</sub>
- **Status:** deceased  <sub>[v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030), [v3 c14 P37](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0037)</sub>
- **Role:** teacher  <sub>[v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060)</sub>

## Appearance

Opal was widely regarded as the most beautiful girl at the Regent's Academy and possessed a striking, radiant appearance. She had large, vivid blue eyes, radiant skin, a full and eye-catching figure, and long blonde hair that she wore in a plait or styled with red geraniums. After her death, her features took on a hallowed, delicate grace and faultless silhouette.

_Sources: [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v3 c14 P31](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0031)_

## Personality

Opal possessed a sunny, pleasant disposition and was prone to frequent laughter and enjoyment of life's lighthearted aspects. She was sentimental, romantic, and preoccupied with thoughts of suitors, male attention, and beaus. In moments of panic or high emotion, she was easily driven to hysterics and weeping.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v1 c23 P16](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0016), [v1 c26 P6](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0006), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059)_

## History

Opal grew up in Brierley and attended the local school, where she frequently expressed her childhood ambition to keep a swarm of suitors dangling once she grew older. She was an active member of the school's Story Club alongside her friends Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Odette Pullen. After completing her studies at Regent's Academy, she secured a position as a teacher at the Delford school. During her young adulthood, she attracted many romantic admirers, rejecting proposals from suitors like Nelson Atkins and the Tullyvale schoolmaster while favoring others such as Herb Tranter. However, following a bout of congestion during the winter, Opal developed galloping consumption, forcing her to step down from teaching despite her hopes of taking a position at Pale Sands. During her illness, she reconciled with her former childhood friend Em White and confided her fears of dying and leaving earth to Nell. She passed away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter and was buried in Brierley.

_Sources: [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056), [v3 c8 P3](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0003), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c11 P8](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0008), [v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053), [v3 c12 P10](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0010), [v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013), [v3 c14 P15](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0015), [v3 c14 P23](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0023), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)_

## Background by volume

- had numerous older sisters who married rapidly  <sub>[v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c26 P17](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0017)</sub>

- hiding in a hallway pantry when her sister Tabitha received a marriage proposal  <sub>[v1 c26 P17](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0017)</sub>

## Quotes

> Floating downward does not bother me when two or three of us are occupying the flat and we are able to sit upright. During those times, it is enjoyable. However, lying flat and acting as if I were deceased—that is something I simply could not do. Fear would actually kill me.  <sub>[v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001)</sub>

> Oh, she appears truly deceased. It fills me with fear, girls. Is it really proper for us to perform in this manner, do you think? Mrs. Sowerby claims that any drama-acting is dreadfully sinful.  <sub>[v1 c28 P13](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0013)</sub>

> I will not be here Tuesday or Wednesday nights. A concert is taking place in Delford, followed by a gathering at Pale Sands. Herb Tranter is escorting me. He is my newest flame. Do not fail to visit me tomorrow. I am eager to have a proper conversation with you. I wish to know everything regarding your activities in Wexcombe.  <sub>[v3 c11 P8](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0008)</sub>

> Because—because—oh, Nell, I am not scared that I will fail to get into heaven. I belong to the church. But—everything there is going to be so unfamiliar. I ponder—and ponder—and it makes me so scared—and—and—homesick. Of course, heaven has to be extremely beautiful, as the Bible states—however, Nell, it will not be like what I am accustomed to.  <sub>[v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013)</sub>

> I can’t help it. Even if what you say about heaven is true—and you can’t be sure—it may be only that imagination of yours—it won’t be just the same. It can’t be. I want to go on living here. I’m so young, Nell. I haven’t had my life. I’ve fought so hard to live—and it isn’t any use—I have to die—and leave everything I care for.  <sub>[v3 c14 P15](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0015)</sub>
